name: BROKEN TOP BOTTLE SHOP & ALE CAFE

fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Front Driveway; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Open Lawn Area; Detached Structure; Perimeter Fencing; Access Drive; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Large Vehicle Parking Area; Limited Rear Access; Vegetation Near Structure; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly from the road.
• Mark the access point to the rear of the property so responders can identify it without searching.
• Keep the rear access gate unlocked or secured with a breakaway lock to allow entry without delay.
• Trim vegetation growing close to the detached structure to keep it clear for responder movement around the building.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of parked vehicles along the path between the main residence and detached structure to allow emergency equipment to move between buildings.
• Post the secondary access drive entry with a visible marker so arriving units can identify it as an alternative route onto the property.

wildfire.conditions: Scattered Trees; Tree Cluster; Scattered Shrubs; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Terrain; Multiple Access Routes; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Grass Cover
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim tree branches that hang directly over or within a few feet of the structure.
• Thin trees within the cluster nearest the structure to create gaps between the canopies.
• Remove shrubs that are growing directly against or touching the structure's exterior walls.
• Cut grass close to the structure and keep it short, particularly during dry periods.
• Clear any dead grass or dry plant material that has accumulated against the foundation or base of walls.
• Maintain open separation between scattered shrubs and the structure by removing shrubs that have grown into the transition zone between the yard and the building.
• Keep branches from scattered trees trimmed up from the ground to reduce the ability of low flames to reach the tree canopy.
• Remove dead branches from trees near the structure before they fall and accumulate on the ground.
• Keep the areas between tree clusters and shrubs clear of dry grass and loose dead plant material.
